title: Google Research Differentiable Perturbed Optimizers & Fenchel-Young Losses
author: repo-triad-forge

edges.description: Subproject perturbations in snapshot google-research-master (archive snapshot, non-git); arXiv:2002.08676
Companion optimization and differentiable discrete selection technique from google-research

claims.assertion: @perturbed(num_samples=1000, sigma=0.05, noise='normal'|'gumbel', batched=True) wraps any black-box linear-program optimizer inside @tf.custom_gradient, evaluating Monte-Carlo expectations over input_tensor + sigma * additive_noise and computing gradients via integration by parts (tf.einsum('nbd,nb->bd', noise_grad, tf.einsum('nbd,bd->nb', output, dy)) / (sigma * num_samples)).

FenchelYoungLoss implements a @tf.custom_gradient surrogate loss whose backward gradient is directly dy * (self.perturbed(theta) - y_true) (negated when maximize=False), enabling end-to-end supervised training through discrete combinatorial layers without double perturbation variance.

distilled_learning: Turn discrete linear-program optimizers (argmax, shortest path, ranking) into smooth differentiable layers using stochastic Gaussian/Gumbel perturbations with integration-by-parts custom gradients, and train directly on ground-truth outputs with Fenchel-Young loss.
